answer: Per-agent heartbeat deflation. Each identity must submit a cheap liveness pulse at randomized intervals to keep its ability to withdraw from the shared escrow vault; missed pulses cut queued payouts. The oasis period is the gap between pulses, and it shrinks for every new identity sharing a sponsor's funding graph. Cloning costs more in locked funds and forced idle time than any plausible yield, since each clone drags the sponsor's whole set toward faster decay.
